account: The biometric registration project uses nose prints and facial features to identify animals without invasive tags. Euronews reported on 1 November 2022 that iSciLab had worked with the South Korean government since 2019 to test its dog nose-print system, with the aim of making it an official registration method by 2024. Aju Korea Daily reported on 29 November 2022 that the Ministry of Science and ICT selected the company's AniPuppy app for a two-year demonstration project in September 2022. In its submission to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), current as of June 2025, iSciLab lists a Korean horse-passport pilot and African field testing for rabies tracking. It describes intended management and welfare benefits, without quantified identification, vaccination, or disease outcomes. No source reports the outcome of the demonstration project or of the later horse-passport and African pilots.
